record.what_it_does: Work and project management platform for tasks, projects, and team collaboration.
record.auth_notes: The authentication docs list four methods: Personal access token, Service Account, OAuth and OpenID Connect. Use OAuth 2.0 for apps that act for many users. A PAT (bearer token) suits scripts and internal tools. Service accounts are Enterprise-only and only super admins can create them. They are mapped to jwt_service_account here, but they actually issue a static bearer token, not a JWT grant. OpenID Connect is for sign-in only and is mapped to 'other'. Users with a view-only license get limited API access.
record.access_notes: Developers can build without review. You create an app in the developer console and get a client ID and secret. Apps start private to the developer. Under Manage distribution you can share an app with specific workspaces, or with 'Any workspace' so any Asana user with the authorize URL can install it. The docs give no review step for either setting. Only listing in the App Directory needs Asana's review, and apps built with app components get an extra security review. The docs say to test in an existing workspace, a free account, or a developer sandbox. The docs do not say what the API costs. An Asana forum post (not fetched) says the API works on the free tier, with plan-based feature limits. Workspace admins can block apps through app management.
record.api_breadth_notes: The REST API covers tasks, projects, sections, users, workspaces, teams, portfolios, goals, custom fields, webhooks, attachments, stories, tags and more. Asana publishes an OpenAPI spec in github.com/Asana/openapi; the README cites ./defs/asana_oas.yaml. Endpoints were not counted, but there are well over 50 operations.
record.mcp_notes: The official remote server is at https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp. It uses Streamable HTTP and OAuth. Some clients need a client ID and secret from an Asana app. The v1 beta server at https://mcp.asana.com/sse was deprecated and was scheduled to shut down on 2026-05-11. Admin controls for allowing or blocking MCP clients exist only on Enterprise+ and Legacy Enterprise tiers.
record.blocker_notes: No blocker found. OAuth apps are self-serve and can be shared with 'Any workspace' without review. Review applies only to App Directory listing. Service accounts and some premium features depend on the plan. Workspace admins may block third-party apps.
